question.text: Two identical charged particles each having a mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> and charge <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow></msup><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> are placed on a horizontal table with a separation of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>L</mi></math> between them such that they stay in limited equilibrium. If the coefficient of friction between each particle and the table is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>25</mn></math>, find the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>L</mi></math>. [Use <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi>ms</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math> ]

solution.text:
Normal reaction applied by table on object will be, N=mg.

Both charges are same, hence a repulsive force will act between them.

Value of force acting will be, kQ2L2.

Now the maximum value of friction force which table can provide is,

=μN=μmg

For equilibrium, kQ2L2=μmg.

L=kQ2μmg=k0.25mgQ=2kmgQ

=29×10910×10-3×102×10-7=0.12 m=12 cm
